rest.gateway.answers.noToken: A route Kong verifies, and the request carries no token. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
rest.gateway.answers.multipleTokens: A route Kong verifies, and the request carries two different tokens. Kong reads the `Authorization` header and also a `jwt` query parameter; send the token in `Authorization` only.
rest.gateway.answers.badToken: A route Kong verifies, and the token is not a JWT it can decode: its parts are not base64url JSON (`invalid JSON`), its `alg` is missing or unknown (`invalid alg`), or its claims or signature are missing.
rest.gateway.answers.noIssuer: A route Kong verifies, and the token has no `iss` claim. With an empty `iss` the message is `Invalid 'iss' in claims`.
rest.gateway.answers.unknownIssuer: A route Kong verifies, and the token's `iss` is not identity's issuer: the token was not issued by Kinetix.
rest.gateway.answers.algorithm: A route Kong verifies, and the token is not signed with `RS256`, the only algorithm identity uses.
rest.gateway.answers.signature: A route Kong verifies, and the signature does not match identity's public key: the token was altered, or signed by another key.
rest.gateway.answers.expired: A route Kong verifies, and the token's `exp` has passed. Refresh the token pair and send the request again with the new access token.
rest.gateway.answers.noExpiry: A route Kong verifies, and the token has no numeric `exp` claim.
rest.gateway.answers.staffNetwork: An admin-only route, called from outside Kinetix's staff network. The admin-only routes are, with every method and everything below them: `/api/v1/sellers/applications`, `/api/v1/sellers/{id}/verify`, `/api/v1/sellers/{id}/reject`, `/api/v1/couriers/applications`, `/api/v1/couriers/{principalId}/approve`, `/api/v1/warehouse/bins`, `/api/v1/warehouse/stock_receipts`, `/api/v1/warehouse/stock_adjustments`, `/api/v1/matching/drivers`, `/api/v1/matching/backoffice`, `/api/v1/orders/sagas`, `/api/v1/orders/returns/needs-attention`, `/api/v1/orders/returns/{returnNumber}/reject` and `/api/v1/orders/{orderNumber}/complete`; `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/api/v1/categories` (`GET` stays open); and `/bff/` on `backoffice.wildanfrananda.my.id`. Kong decides by the caller's network alone, before the service is asked: a valid admin token does not change the answer, and neither does a retry from the same network. On identity's and matching's admin routes Kong checks the token first, so a request without a valid token gets one of the `401`s above instead. A refused request does not count against the rate limit.
rest.gateway.answers.noRoute: A request to the API host whose path matches no route, or whose method a method-restricted route does not allow. The service is never reached.
rest.gateway.answers.appHost: A request to `seller.wildanfrananda.my.id` or `backoffice.wildanfrananda.my.id` for any path outside `/bff/`, `/bff` itself and every `/api/v1/` path included. The web apps' hosts serve only the edge: a browser calls the API as `/bff/api/v1/…` on its own host, and any other client calls `api.wildanfrananda.my.id`.
rest.gateway.answers.tooLarge: An upload to the storage host whose body is larger than 16 MB. With `Expect: 100-continue` the status is `417` and the message the same.
rest.gateway.answers.rateLimited: More than 100 requests within one minute from one client address to one of Kong's routes. Each route keeps its own count: a route holds one service's paths, sometimes several prefixes of it, and the admin-only paths, `/health`, `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/bff/` on each web app's host count on their own. The Midtrans notification route allows 600 a minute. The count starts again at the beginning of each clock minute, and `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until then. Every answer to a counted request carries `RateLimit-Remaining`, so a client can slow down before it is refused. Kong's `401`s and the `403` of the staff network are refused before counting and do not count.
rest.gateway.answers.badUpstream: The service refused the connection or sent a response Kong could not read. The format follows the request's `Accept` header, then its `Content-Type`; with neither, the body is plain text as shown, and with `Accept: application/json` it is Kong's JSON error.
rest.gateway.answers.serviceDown: The service is not running, so its name does not resolve. Nothing reached the service; the request can be sent again later.
rest.gateway.answers.timeout: The service did not answer in time. The request may still have taken effect: read the current state before sending a request that changes something again. The body's format is chosen as for `502`.
rest.gateway.health.summary: Answers that the gateway is up. Kong answers it itself; no service is called.
rest.gateway.health.case.up: Always, while Kong is running. It says nothing about the services behind it.
rest.gateway.securityTxt.summary: The API's security contact in the RFC 9116 format: where to report a vulnerability, the policy that applies, the languages a report may be written in, and until when the file is valid. Kong answers it itself; no service is called.
rest.gateway.securityTxt.case.served: Always. `Contact` is where to report a vulnerability, privately; `Policy` is the page that says how reports are handled; `Canonical` is the file's own address. The file is not valid after `Expires`; read it again rather than keep a copy.
